correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2, the grounded graph Laplacian is I+L(Q_n). Its positive radial heat kernel yields strictly positive h_j and differences h_j-h_{j+1}, justifying every absolute current sign. Binomial moment identities S=1/3 and T=1/5 give exact cut-column norms 1+n/3 (spokes) and (6n+14)/15 (cube). Exact diagonals a_n and 2(1-a_n)/n give complementary columns. The cycle-column difference is negative at n=2,3,4 and positive at n=5; n>=6 follows from a_n>1/(n+1). Every edge belongs to one of the two orbits. The standalone Python/SymPy checker confirmed 30 finite dimensions by rational spectral identities and five grounded inverse problems (444 edges total); finite cases are corroborative, and infinite validity rests on the integrals and inequalities in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The two-orbit norm classification addresses a natural infinite family created by a canonical graph operation on Hamming cubes. The precise common dimension-five boundary links a strict switch of maximizing cycle-projection edge orbit with a strict reversal in how apex insertion changes the cut-projection norm, neither of which follows from the ordinary-cube norm or a universal bound. The exact mean current length supplies a logarithmic-size growth example in electrical-flow localization, with clear motivation beyond a single incidental rational computation.
